## A heatmap from GTEx

The report uses 13 genes and eight tissues. Gene symbols are human-readable names;
GTEx needs a **versioned GENCODE ID**. Keep `datasetId=gtex_v8` in both requests.

1. In `params: genes:` in the report header, inspect the core gene list.
2. Read `/reference/gene?geneId=KRT14&datasetId=gtex_v8` from the
   [GTEx API](https://gtexportal.org/api/v2/reference/gene?geneId=KRT14&datasetId=gtex_v8).
   Extract `data$gencodeId`; do not guess the suffix after the dot.
3. Query `/expression/medianGeneExpression` with that `gencodeId` and `datasetId`.
   The given fetch code requests all tissues once per gene and then retains eight.
4. The saved CSV has `gene`, `gencode_id`, `tissue`, `tpm`, `dataset`.
   Plot `gene` against `tissue`, with fill `log10(tpm + 1)`, using `geom_tile()`.
   Label the colour key **log10(TPM + 1)**. RNA abundance is not protein abundance.
5. Re-knit with `params$genes` changed to TUBB, TUBB3 and TUBB4A. A parameter is an
   input to the report, not a manually edited result.

## A trial chart from ClinicalTrials.gov

1. Use [the API query](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.intr=mavacamten&format=json&pageSize=100&countTotal=true).
   `query.intr` searches interventions; this can return studies with multiple interventions.
2. Read `studies`, then each `protocolSection`. Extract NCT ID, title, conditions,
   status and `designModule$phases`. Follow `nextPageToken` until absent.
3. A study may list two phases; the CSV joins them with `;`. Split these before counting.
   Keep studies without a drug-development phase as **Not applicable**. A study counted
   in two phase categories is still one study.
4. Plot the number of study records by phase with `geom_col()`. This shows research
   activity, not treatment efficacy. Keep cancelled/completed/recruiting status separate.

## Tasks

**T4.** Which selected tissues are high for KRT14, DES, GFAP and MYH7? `[ELO 6]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
In the shipped GTEx v8 snapshot: **KRT14 → skin**, **DES → skeletal muscle**, **GFAP → brain cortex**, **MYH7 → heart left ventricle**. KRT14 is also abundant in oesophageal mucosa. These are tissue medians from mixed cell populations, so a high value does not prove every cell expresses the gene.
:::

**T5.** Why use log10(TPM + 1)? Why are NEFL and GFAP different markers even when both are high in brain? `[ELO 6]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
The log scale compresses large abundance differences; adding 1 permits zeros. NEFL is associated with neuronal intermediate filaments, GFAP with astrocytic glial filaments. Bulk tissue cannot resolve which cell contributes the RNA; follow up with HPA single-cell evidence.
:::

**T6. [VG]** Compare trial phases and re-knit with a new gene set. What changed, and what can neither plot establish? `[ELO 6, 9]`

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Answer (checked 2026-11-18)"}
The trial snapshot contains phase 1, 2, 3 and 4 records plus studies without an applicable phase; one record combines phases 2 and 3. The count changes as the registry updates. A new gene set changes expression patterns, but neither expression nor trial counts alone establish a mechanism, clinical benefit, or safety. State your own parameter values and the actual result.
:::

## Finish the report

Include both labelled plots, two short biological interpretations, one inline R
number, the dataset/retrieval date, the API URLs and `sessionInfo()`. Knit to HTML
and check for errors. Do not interpret small differences between tissues as significant
without donor-level variation and a suitable analysis.
